title: Review: Translation; Transcription; Post-transcriptional control and RNAi
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: GE04a#t1 term and clue written for the game; GE05b#t2 term and clue written for the game; GE04a#t2 term and clue written for the game; GE05b#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: GE04a#N.11, GE04b#N.4b, GE05b#N.13b, GR03#N.12a, GE04a#N.3b, GE04b#N.6c, GE05b#N.7b, GR03#N.8, GE04b#N.8, GE05b#N.4b. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Transcription
items.clue: Making an RNA copy of a gene from one DNA strand; the first stage of gene expression.

items.label: Elongation
items.clue: Stage in which tRNAs bring amino acids codon by codon, each transferred to the growing chain.

items.label: RNA polymerase
items.clue: Enzyme that binds at the start of a gene and joins adjacent nucleotides of the new transcript.

items.label: Rough ER
items.clue: Membrane system with ribosomes bound to its cytoplasmic surface; polypeptides made there enter it.

questions.stem: α-Amanitin, a toxin from the death cap mushroom, blocks the RNA polymerase that makes mRNA in eukaryotic cells. It has no effect on DNA polymerase or on ribosomes. Which prediction about liver cells exposed to it is correct?

options.text: DNA replication stops, because the cells can no longer separate their DNA strands.
Translation of mRNA already in the cytoplasm stops at once.
No new mRNA is made, so protein synthesis falls as the existing mRNA is broken down.
The DNA of the cells' genes is damaged, so their base sequences change.

questions.explanation: Without RNA polymerase there is no transcription and no new mRNA. Proteins are made only until the existing mRNA runs out.

questions.stem: Which statement describes promoters and enhancers?

options.text: They are proteins that bind to DNA and help RNA polymerase to begin the transcription of a gene.
They are parts of a gene's coding sequence that are transcribed and then translated into the protein.
They are DNA sequences that must lie upstream of a gene, before its transcription start site.
They are stretches of DNA that RNA polymerase and transcription factors bind to when transcription begins.

questions.explanation: Promoters and enhancers are regulatory DNA sequences; RNA polymerase and transcription factors bind them to initiate transcription.

questions.stem: A hypothetical drug acts on ribosomes that are not attached to an mRNA, preventing them from assembling on an mRNA at its start codon. Which prediction is most likely shortly after the drug is added to a culture of eukaryotic cells?

options.text: Polypeptides go on being made, as amino acids can pair with the mRNA codons directly.
Cells switch to another way of making polypeptides to obtain the proteins they need.
Polypeptides already being made are completed, but no new ones are started.
No new mRNA is made, since ribosomes can no longer copy the DNA into mRNA.

questions.explanation: Ribosomes already in elongation continue to the stop codon and release their polypeptides, but no new initiation can occur.

questions.stem: A mutation inside an intron of a gene changes how the primary mRNA is spliced: exon 4 is now removed along with the introns. Exon 4 is exactly 60 bases long, and the base sequences of all the exons are unchanged. What is the effect?

options.text: The mature mRNA lacks exon 4, so the protein lacks the amino acids coded by exon 4.
No effect on the protein, because introns are removed anyway and only exons code for it.
Exon 4 has been deleted from the gene's DNA, so it can never be used in any cell.
The intron is now translated in place of exon 4, giving a protein of the same length.

questions.stem: Which statement describes how the DNA of a gene is used during transcription?

options.text: One of the two DNA strands is used as a template, and the RNA made is complementary to it.
Both of the DNA strands are used as templates, and the two RNA strands made then pair together.
One of the two DNA strands is used as a template, and the RNA made is identical to it.
One of the two DNA strands is converted into RNA, which then leaves the nucleus for the cytoplasm.

questions.explanation: RNA polymerase reads one template strand and adds complementary RNA nucleotides (U opposite A). The RNA has the same sequence as the other strand, with U for T.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the processing of a primary transcript into mature mRNA in a eukaryotic cell?

options.text: A GTP cap and a poly-A tail are added to the transcript, and its introns are removed.
A GTP cap and a poly-A tail are added to the gene's DNA, and its introns are then removed.
The introns, the GTP cap and the poly-A tail are all removed before the mRNA is translated.
A GTP cap and a poly-A tail are added, and the introns are kept so that they can be translated.

questions.explanation: A GTP cap is added to the 5′ end, a poly-A tail to the 3′ end, and the introns are excised and the exons spliced together.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes how translation of an mRNA ends?

options.text: A tRNA pairs with the stop codon and adds a last amino acid that seals the chain.
The ribosome reaches the last nucleotide of the mRNA and lets go of the chain.
When a stop codon is reached, the completed polypeptide is released.
The ribosome releases the amino acids, which then join to form the polypeptide.

questions.explanation: Translation continues codon by codon until a stop codon is reached. No amino acid is added for it, and the polypeptide is released from the ribosome.

questions.stem: Researchers add an siRNA whose base sequence is complementary to part of the mRNA of gene K. Which prediction is correct?

options.text: The base sequence of gene K changes, so gene K no longer codes for its protein.
Gene K is still transcribed, but its mRNA is cut, so less K protein is made.
Gene K stops being transcribed, because siRNA controls gene expression at transcription.
The siRNA is translated into a protein that binds gene K's mRNA and blocks its translation.

questions.explanation: The siRNA base-pairs with the matching mRNA, which is cut. Transcription carries on; translation of K mRNA is prevented.

questions.stem: Using the β-globin gene data, what percentage of the pre-mRNA is kept in the mature mRNA?

When a hypothetical species of bacterium is moved to a new food source, molecules of a newly needed enzyme can be detected sooner after transcription of its gene begins than in a comparable eukaryotic cell. Which explanation best accounts for this difference?

options.text: Bacterial ribosomes read the gene's DNA directly, so no mRNA needs to be made.
Bacterial ribosomes on the rough ER sit near the nucleus, so the mRNA travels only a short way.
Bacterial ribosomes make the mRNA themselves and then translate it straight away.
Bacterial ribosomes begin translating an mRNA before its transcription is complete.
